title: Nepal's Gen Z Uprising Is A Bigger Deal Than You Think
content:
This Wednesday is the one year anniversary of when I quit my job to go full time independent. It’s clearer than ever that we need a robust independent media ecosystem to hold power to account, and the only reason I’m able to do the work I do (not just this newsletter, but my bi-weekly videos, my Free Speech Friday series educating people on civil liberties, my podcast, my social media content, my tech policy and civil rights advocacy work, and so much more)— is because of those of you who pay to support this newsletter. I can’t even begin to explain how grateful I am.

Since the vast majority of my paid subscribers signed up right after I went independent, these next couple months are extremely make it or break it. I hope that if you like my work, you’ll renew your subscription or purchase a paid one and give me the opportunity to remain independent for another year. 🙏

(If you prefer not to subscribe on Substack btw, I’m also now on Patreon). Thank you again so much for everything. And if you have any suggestions on what you’d like to see more of from me, let me know!

Subscribe now

Nearly a month ago peaceful student demonstrators protesting corruption in Nepal were shot and killed, sparking nationwide outrage. Government buildings were set in fire, leaders were forced out, and the prime minister resigned, leaving the country’s future uncertain. But that’s not how the mainstream media reported it.

Major U.S. news outlets misrepresented Nepal’s Gen Z youth movement, portraying young protesters as spoiled children upset about losing social media access, rather than as citizens fighting corruption and authoritarian suppression of free speech.

It was a lot of the same framing that the media has used over other authoritarian crackdowns on speech like the TikTok ban here in the U.S.

To break down exactly what is happening in Nepal, I brought on Bala Krishna Sah, one of the top journalists in Nepal, who writes for The Himalayan Times, the country’s number one English language newspaper. He joins me to reveal the real story, that you won’t see in western media, and to talk about why the free speech fight happening in Nepal has global implications. WATCH HERE.

User Mag news rundown

  • “Cozy cardio” is a new TikTok trend where people are wearing fuzzy socks and lighting candles to do intense cardio workouts.

  • Costco is selling a 5-foot-tall chocolate advent calendar.

  • There is a woman in San Francisco who charges $30k to name your baby.

  • Ben Stiller launched a soda brand.

  • Around a third of US adults say they get news from podcasts at least sometimes, up from 22% in 2020; 6% say they paid for news podcasts in the past 12 months.

  • Meta AI launched “Vibes” an entire feed for short AI-generated slop videos.

  • Elon Musk’s Grok AI has been cleared for use in U.S. government agencies.

  • As AI threatens white-collar work, more young Americans are choosing blue-collar careers.

  • Chick-fil-A is launching a Starbucks competitor called Daybright, scheduled to open in Atlanta this fall.

  • A group of tech YouTubers made a fleet of AI powered trash-catching trash cans. The video is incredible.

  • Lindsay Halligan, the newly-installed US Attorney prosecuting James Comey, is an insurance attorney and a Miss Colorado finalist. She has never prosecuted a case.

  • Moflin, little fuzzy AI pets that develop a personality over time, are going viral in Japan. (They are so cute).

  • TikTokers are obsessed with “heavy soda” aka soda with extra syrup. You can add extra syrup to make a heavy soda version of brands like Sprite, Dr Pepper, Mountain Dew, and more.

  • Nexstar caved and now Jimmy Kimmel is back on the air in all markets.

  • YouTube is testing AI hosts, who will share stories and trivia about the music users are listening to.

  • Instacart published their fall candy and decor trends. Reese’s Peanut butter cups are still people’s top Halloween candy.

  • The Black woman who went viral for going undercover on LinkedIn as a white woman named Emily to expose racial bias in corporate hiring is making a full length documentary about being Black in corporate America.

  • A travel YouTuber ended up live-vlogging Nepal’s revolution.

  • DOGE fired so many GSA staff that 131 federal leases expired without the government actually vacating the properties. Taxpayers are now on the hook for steep penalty fees from the landlords.

  • Woman Twitch Streamers are afraid to go to TwitchCon this year due to safety concerns over crazy fans.

  • Joe Kelly is the hairstylist saving the big, sexy blowout.

  • People on TikTok hate “cool girls” but all want to be “cool aunts.”

  • Sephora is The Rockettes’ first official beauty retailer partner.

  • Drew Barrymore’s makeup line shut down.

  • Million-year-old skull found in China could rewrite human evolution timeline, study finds: “This changes a lot of thinking”

  • Lifestyle gurus are becoming obsessed with “intentionality” as the latest buzzword.

  • Marc Maron, Shane Gillis, and other comedians are criticizing peers for performing at Saudi Arabia’s state-backed Riyadh Comedy Festival which Human Rights Watch says is an attempt to whitewash the kingdom’s human rights abuses.

  • Decades ago a photographer went around calling the biggest European companies, asking to show up at their office and shoot their boardrooms. This series of photos he took are really pretty.
